ranking.note: Kept P2; placed ahead of #26966 because it is the stated groundwork for parallel indexing and delivers I/O and lock-contention gains on its own.

inconsistencies: Chain: #34489 (batched db writes) is described as groundwork for #26966 (parallel index sync); review #34489 first so the parallelization lands on the batched write path rather than being reworked.

Overlap: #24230 (stop using node internal types / cs_main, sync logic extraction) and #35474 (move index ownership from globals to NodeContext) both attack index/node decoupling for multiprocess (#10102) and will touch the same construction and lookup sites. #24230 is the broader and more consequential change and should set the direction; #35474 should be reviewed against it to avoid duplicated or conflicting restructuring.

Both #34489 and #24230 claim reduced cs_main contention during index sync via different mechanisms (batched ranges vs. removing the lock dependency); reviewers should confirm the two approaches compose rather than one superseding the other.
#35229 (CBlockIndex by reference) touches the same index signatures #24230 rewrites; as a pure janitorial refactor it should yield to the higher-band work rather than force it to rebase.
result.notes: Four genuinely distinct levels are present: two sync-performance PRs plus one architectural decoupling and one capability gap (pruned txindex) at P2; a real but uncommon error-reporting bug, a global-state cleanup, and disk-space housekeeping at P3; a signature-only refactor at P4. No band changes were needed — the standalone assessments were mutually consistent; only the order within P2 changed to respect the #34489 → #26966 dependency.
